mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a robustness check across multiple rate hike cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE turns insignificant (p > 0.05) in a multiple regression, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but proxy via HOUST for industrial demand) combined with a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a shift toward deflationary demand growth, lowering real interest rates and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 1% over the same period
failure_condition: The HOUST-CPIAUCSL interaction is not predictive of 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.05 in a rolling regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests tight supply conditions and reduced upward price pressure, lowering the cost of capital and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a quarter while CPIAUCSL declines by > 0.5% in the same quarter
failure_condition: The combined effect of INDPRO and CPIAUCSL does not predict positive 60-day returns (p-value for test statistic > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Federal Funds rate turns negative (i.e., rates are trending lower), it indicates a shift toward monetary easing that reduces the real interest rate differential with emerging markets, improving the S&P 500's international diversification and driving positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during identified easing phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable but can be inferred from labor market dynamics) combined with a prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor shortage that encourages firms to invest in capital expansion, which elevates earnings growth expectations and produces positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.3 percentage points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Earnings growth forecasts (from S&P Earnings Estimate dataset) do not translate into statistically significant positive 60-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% along with rising retail activity (HOUST) indicates that demand is growing faster than supply while price pressures remain subdued, lowering the real risk-free rate and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for 3 consecutive months and HOUST increases each month
failure_condition: The CPIAUCSL-HOUST interaction is not predictive of 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of high uncertainty (indicated by a sharp increase in volatility proxies not directly available in the provided series, but assumed as context) the S&P 500 tends to exhibit mean-reverting behavior with a short-term upward bias in the 5-day window following a negative news shock, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL shows a sharp one-time monthly drop followed by a month of flat or rising values (used as a proxy for negative外
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in a robustness check across multiple volatility proxies (not available in this catalog).
